{"description":"Design: docs/design/emailpush.md. Decisions: docs/design/DECISIONS.md.
Note key: E9. Crates: jmap-mail-server. Size: M.

Spec: draft-ietf-jmap-emailpush-05 §3: MUST NOT exceed the push service size limit; MUST split across multiple EmailPush objects; add properties in order and on overflow omit that property and all later ones; MUST NOT omit properties unless that Email alone would exceed the limit (jmapio/jmap#476). Design: docs/design/emailpush.md §5.3 steps 3-4, §10 "r44n.2 splitting".

In emailpush/deliver.rs, replace the single-push placeholder in email_pushes_for: pack projected Emails greedily in delivery order, measured with serde_json::to_vec(&EmailPush).len() (the serializer jmap_web_push::Sender::send uses), starting a new EmailPush when appending would exceed batch.max_bytes. Every part carries the same state (the state after the whole batch). An Email that does not fit alone goes out alone, rebuilt by adding properties in list order until the next would exceed max_bytes; that property and all later ones are dropped (strict prefix, no skipping). If an EmailPush holding one {} does not fit, return EmailPushError::LimitTooSmall rather than an oversize push. Document that Web Push without padding allows jmap_web_push::MAX_PLAINTEXT = 3993 bytes.
Acceptance: N small Emails over max_bytes => at least 2 pushes, every Email complete, each push <= max_bytes by serde_json::to_vec; a lone oversized Email goes alone as a strict prefix; a large property 2 followed by a tiny property 3 drops both; a small Email next to an oversized one is not truncated; a tiny limit => LimitTooSmall.","notes":"2026-11-13: refiled from docs/design/emailpush.md (note key E9).","title":"mail-server: split EmailPush across pushes before truncating Email properties"}

Spec: draft-ietf-jmap-emailpush-05 §3: MUST NOT exceed the push service size limit; MUST split across multiple EmailPush objects; add properties in order and on overflow omit that property and all later ones; MUST NOT omit properties unless that Email alone would exceed the limit (jmapio/jmap#476). Design: docs/design/emailpush.md §5.2 (last paragraph), §5.3 steps 3-4, §10 "r44n.2 splitting"; decision 16.

In emailpush/deliver.rs, replace the single-push placeholder in email_pushes_for: pack projected Emails greedily in delivery order, measured with serde_json::to_vec(&EmailPush).len() (the serializer jmap_web_push::Sender::send uses), starting a new EmailPush when appending would exceed batch.max_bytes. Every part carries the same state (the state after the whole batch). An Email that does not fit alone goes out alone, rebuilt by adding properties in list order until the next would exceed max_bytes; that property and all later ones are dropped (strict prefix, no skipping). If an EmailPush holding one {} does not fit, return EmailPushError::LimitTooSmall rather than an oversize push. Document that Web Push without padding allows jmap_web_push::MAX_PLAINTEXT = 3993 bytes. Send-time check (decision 16): before filtering, email_pushes_for decodes the account's stored config and runs E6's pure check_email_push_config against the live EmailPushAccount; a config that fails it gets no push ([]), so a deployment that forgot to call check_email_push_change, or wrote a config directly, never sends one built from an invalid config.
